key_insight: Reducing memory to delayed feedback enables optimistic constrained online optimization with guarantees that adapt to environmental change and prediction accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The framework is relevant to stateful online learning and non-stochastic control where decisions affect future costs and must respect time-varying budget constraints.
method: Reduce memory-dependent optimization to delayed feedback using state-dependent gradients.
Incorporate untrusted predictions into an optimistic algorithm without requiring functional separability.
Bound dynamic regret and cumulative constraint violation using path length and prediction accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical rather than empirical evidence: perfect predictions yield O(1) regret, with cumulative constraint violation O(√T) for unknown path length and O(log T) for known or online-observable path length.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees depend on prediction accuracy and path-length information; practical runtime and empirical performance are not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Dynamic Optimistic Constrained OCO with Memory via Delay Equivalence
